facts: A dashed line drawn to split a figure is a construction line only — it has no area of its own.
A length that is not marked can often be found from the marked lengths, because opposite sides of the overall rectangle must match.
Keep the units consistent, and give the answer in square units ($\text{m}^{2}$, $\text{cm}^{2}$).
steps: Split the composite shape into simple shapes.
Calculate the area of each simple shape.

workedExamples.solution_text:
The triangle shares the rectangle's $9\text{ m}$ side.
$\begin{align*}A_1&=9\times4\\&=36\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_2&=\frac12\times9\times2\\&=9\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1+A_2\\&=36+9\\&=45\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

The semicircle has diameter $4\text{ m}$, so its radius is $2\text{ m}$.
$\begin{align*}A_1&=4\times3\\&=12\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$A_2=\frac12\pi(2)^2=2\pi\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1+A_2\\&=12+2\pi\\&\approx18.28\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular yard is $15\text{ m}$ by $10\text{ m}$. A rectangular patio is $4\text{ m}$ by $3\text{ m}$, and a separate triangular flower bed has base $6\text{ m}$ and perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$. Calculate the remaining area of the yard.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Subtract both areas from the whole yard.
$A_1=15\times10=150\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=4\times3=12\text{ m}^2$
$A_3=\frac12\times6\times3=9\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1-A_2-A_3\\&=150-12-9\\&=129\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A path of constant width $1\text{ m}$ surrounds a rectangular garden $7\text{ m}$ long and $4\text{ m}$ wide. Calculate the area of the path.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Add the path width at both ends of each garden dimension.
$L=7+2(1)=9\text{ m}$
$W=4+2(1)=6\text{ m}$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_{\text{outer}}-A_{\text{garden}}\\&=9\times6-7\times4\\&=54-28\\&=26\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A semicircle of diameter $4\text{ m}$ is cut from one side of a rectangular sheet $9\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$. Calculate the remaining area to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
The semicircle has radius $4\div2=2\text{ m}$.
$A_1=9\times5=45\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=\frac12\pi(2)^2=2\pi\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1-A_2\\&=45-2\pi\\&\approx38.72\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

The semicircle has radius $3\div2=1.5\text{ m}$.
$A_1=7\times4=28\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=3\times2=6\text{ m}^2$
$A_3=\frac12\pi(1.5)^2=1.125\pi\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1-A_2-A_3\\&=28-6-1.125\pi\\&\approx18.47\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A racetrack lies between two ovals. Each oval consists of a rectangle with a semicircle on each short side. Both rectangles are $24\text{ m}$ long. Their widths are $16\text{ m}$ and $10\text{ m}$, and each semicircle's diameter equals its rectangle's width. Calculate the track area to $2$ decimal places.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Each pair of semicircles forms one circle. The outer radius is $8\text{ m}$ and the inner radius is $5\text{ m}$.
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{outer}}&=24\times16+\pi(8)^2\\&=384+64\pi\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A_{\text{inner}}&=24\times10+\pi(5)^2\\&=240+25\pi\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_{\text{outer}}-A_{\text{inner}}\\&=(384+64\pi)-(240+25\pi)\\&=144+39\pi\\&\approx266.52\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$

workedExamples.question_text: A garden consists of a rectangle $11\text{ m}$ by $5\text{ m}$ with a triangle of perpendicular height $3\text{ m}$ joined along its $11\text{ m}$ side. Each bag of mulch covers $6\text{ m}^2$. Only whole bags can be bought. How many bags are needed?
workedExamples.solution_text:
$A_1=11\times5=55\text{ m}^2$
$A_2=\frac12\times11\times3=16.5\text{ m}^2$
$\begin{align*}A&=A_1+A_2\\&=55+16.5\\&=71.5\text{ m}^2\end{align*}$
$71.5\div6=11.9166\ldots$
Round up to cover the whole garden: $12$ bags.

$A_1 = 6\times 4$
$= 24\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(3)^{2}$
$= 14.1371\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$

The triangle has base $6$ m and perpendicular height $4$ m.
$A_1 = 12\times 8$

$A_2 = \frac{1}{2}\times 6\times 4$

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular wall is $8\text{ m}$ wide and $5\text{ m}$ high. An arch is cut from the wall. The arch consists of a rectangle $4\text{ m}$ wide and $3\text{ m}$ high, with a semicircle of diameter $4\text{ m}$ joined to its top.
Calculate the remaining area of the wall, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
The semicircle has radius $2\text{ m}$.
$A_1 = 8\times 5$
$= 40\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = 4\times 3$
$= 12\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_3 = \frac{1}{2}\pi(2)^{2}$
$= 6.2831\ldots\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 - A_2 - A_3$
$= 21.72\text{ m}^{2}$

mastery.question_text:
A racetrack is the region between two ovals. Each oval consists of a rectangle with a semicircle joined to each short side. Both rectangles are $30\text{ m}$ long. The outer rectangle is $18\text{ m}$ wide and the inner rectangle is $12\text{ m}$ wide. Each semicircle's diameter equals the width of its rectangle.
Calculate the area of the racetrack, correct to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
The two outer semicircles form a circle of radius $9\text{ m}$. The two inner semicircles form a circle of radius $6\text{ m}$.
$A_1 = 30\times 18 + \pi(9)^{2}$
$= 540 + 81\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$A_2 = 30\times 12 + \pi(6)^{2}$
$= 360 + 36\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$A = A_1 - A_2$
$= 180 + 45\pi\text{ m}^{2}$
$= 321.37\text{ m}^{2}$
